about: Proofs of open problems accepted by Lean are merged and credited at once. They count as an open problem solved only once the formal statement has been checked against the original problem (confirmed). flagged: the formal statement does not say what the problem says, so the open problem is not solved. known: listed as open upstream, but already settled in the literature (the Lean proof is a formalization of a known result).

Erdos1066.erdos_1066.variants.higher_dim.note: This is a genuine disproof by construction. It uses a Kerdock-set (Kantor-Williams) two-angle configuration in dimension d=3q (q=2^(2t+1)) with n=2q^2 points. All squared norms are b and all inner products are +-a, with b=1/2+a, so the minimum distance is 1. A Gram-sum argument shows that any subset with all pairwise distances >1 has at most k+2 ~ sqrt(2q)+2 points, whereas c*n/d = 2cq/3; this refutes any uniform constant c. gDim faithfully encodes Erdős's g_d(n). The 'constant independent of d and n' reading is the only meaningful one: erdosproblems.com itself calls the upper bound g_d(n) << n/d 'trivial' via widely spaced simplices, and for fixed d the bound holds with a d-dependent constant (kissing number). erdosproblems.com/1066 is open, with 0 proof claims and no forum comment on the higher-dimensional question. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA110566.conjecture.note: The disproof shows 81 (indeed any multiple of 81) never occurs. v_3(a(n)) = floor(log_3 n) + v_3(H(n)). Using the 3-adic splitting H(n) = H(n/3)/3 + (3-integral part) (cf. Shiu, arXiv:1607.02863), the proof shows v_3(H(n)) + log_3 n <= 3 for all n >= 27, and checks 27 <= n < 81 directly. I independently confirmed numerically that max v_3(a(n)) = 3 for n < 3000 and that 27 occurs but 81 does not. The definition matches OEIS (a(1..6) = 1,1,1,1,1,3), and the conjecture (Jianing Song, 2022) is still listed as open in OEIS. The argument is elementary and close to the classical result J_3 = {2,7,22} (Eswarathasan-Levine), but I found no prior record of the refutation. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA189409.conjecture_1.note: The statement 'a(n) = (p_n#)^2+1 is always squarefree' is faithful (offset 0, a(0)=2). The disproof is a direct computational counterexample: a(9) = 223092870^2 + 1 = 49770428644836901 = 29^2 * 59180057841661. I verified this independently, and a(0..8) have no square factor below 10^5. The OEIS entry still says it is 'unknown whether or not numbers in this sequence are always squarefree'. Correct and resolves the stated question, though it is a trivial computational observation rather than a deep result. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA234360.conjecture_1.note: The proof gives an explicit counterexample n=4722, kernel-checked by rfl without native_decide: certified totients for 1..4721, explicit proper divisors for 4329 values of k, and base-2 Fermat non-witnesses (which validly prove compositeness) for the other 392. So a(4722)=0, refuting Sun's 'a(n)>0 for all n>1'. The definition matches OEIS. OEIS records only Adamczewski's refutation of the other clause of Conjecture (i), the phi/2 - k version at n=1408 (arXiv:2608.11941). That paper does not address a(n)>0, and the b-file stops at n=2500. The first clause, which the formal statement isolates, appears to have been open. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA46969.conjecture1.note: The proof establishes the stronger identity a(p) = 12(2p-1) for primes p>3 with 2p-1 prime. It uses von Staudt-Clausen plus Faulhaber/power sums modulo p^2 and q^2 to decide which primes cancel. The conjecture then follows because 2p-1 is prime by hypothesis. The definition (denominator of B_{2n}/(2n(2n-1)), a(1)=12) matches OEIS. The hypotheses (p>3) match 'n>2 in A005382' (p>=7). OEIS still lists Conjecture I as open; only Conjecture II was refuted (Adamczewski). The argument is a classical-style corollary, but I found no prior proof. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

VCDimConvex.hasAddVCNDimAtMost_two_two_o.note: HasAddVCNDimAtMost C 2 2 means no convex C in R^3 can 2-shatter a 3x3 sumset grid a_i+b_j by translates, and the proof shows exactly that. The steps: shattering forbids opposite-sign convex dependencies, so the direction planes of a and b are distinct 2-planes; a normal form follows; then a covering of R^3 minus 0 by four facial cones forces a convex-combination contradiction between two translates. This is a genuine geometric argument, and the statement is the project's own faithful definition. The problem comes from formal-conjectures itself (section 'What's not in the literature', tagged open), not from an external source. Known neighbours are VC_2 <= 1 false (KitaKen1) and a finite bound of 2^{8(n+2)^n}-1 (KitaKen1). I found no prior proof of the bound 2. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture72.con.note: The counterexample has 19 vertices in layers of sizes 7,2,1,2,7: consecutive layers are completely joined, the outer layers are cliques and the inner layers independent. I verified by brute force that the average eccentricity is 70/19, max lambda(v) = 4 (the middle vertex), and the largest induced tree has 5 vertices, while ceil(70/19+4/3) = 6. The definitions (eccent averaged, induced-subgraph indepNum of the neighbourhood, largest induced tree) are faithful to WOWII #72. Caveat: the WOWII site was unreachable from here, so the open status rests on the formal-conjectures transcription ('status O') and a web search that found no earlier refutation. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA208425.conjecture_2.note: The statement is faithful: a(n) = sum C(n,k)C(n-k,k)C(n+k,k) matches the OEIS formula, and because p = 1 (mod 3) the natural-number divisions 2(p-1)/3 and (p-1)/3 are exact. This is Z.-W. Sun's 2016 conjecture (ii), part 1: sum_{k<p} a(k) = C(2(p-1)/3,(p-1)/3) mod p^2. The proof is a genuine argument. It isolates the exceptional term k=r=(p-1)/3, which yields the binomial coefficient mod p^2, and kills the remaining terms with a finite-field identity, sum over k<=(p-1)/2, k != r, of C(2k,k)/(k-r) = 0 in Z/p. The OEIS entry lists it as a conjecture, and Pan-Sun (Front. Comb. Number Theory 2026, arXiv:2012.05121) prove only part (i). No published proof of (ii) turned up in a search, and the PR cites no prior source. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA234360.conjecture_4.note: The target is Sun's conjecture (ii), second part: for n>3, some 0<k<n makes k(k+1)^{phi(n-k)/2}-1 prime. The formalization squares both sides to avoid half-integer exponents. The disproof is a kernel-checked counterexample at n=3998. For 1<=k<=3995 it exhibits an explicit proper divisor or a base-2 Fermat failure of k(k+1)^{phi(3998-k)/2}-1. For k=3996 and 3997, where phi=1, it shows k+1 is not a square, and those two cases also fail under a floor reading (3995 and 3996 are composite), so the counterexample holds under any reasonable reading. Adamczewski (arXiv:2608.11941, the reference in the OEIS comment) disproved only conjecture (i), second part, at n=1408. Formal-conjectures marks that one solved and this one open, so this disproof appears new. It is a modest computational result. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA260194.conjecture.note: The definition matches OEIS A260194 (three initial 1s, then a(n+3) = a(n+2) + gcd(a(n+2), a(n)), shifted to index 0), and the question 'does every positive integer occur as a difference?' is rendered exactly. The disproof is a genuine finite modular certificate. It proves that from any state whose last two differences are 1, every later difference is at most 89 until the state returns to (1,1); the sequence enters such a state at its start, so the difference 90 never occurs. OEIS still lists this as an open question, and no prior answer turned up. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

RefactorableNumber.zelinsky_refactorable.note: The statement is faithful to Zelinsky (J. Integer Seq. 5 (2002), Art. 02.2.8), Conjecture 32: any arithmetic progression of positive integers that contains a tau (refactorable) number contains infinitely many. The formal version is: for every m>=1 and refactorable n0 there is a larger refactorable n with n = n0 mod m. The proof is a real but very short argument: take a prime p > n0 with p = 1 mod m (Dirichlet) and n = n0*p^{p-1}. Then d(n) = d(n0)*p divides n and n = n0 mod m. Wikipedia still lists the question as unsolved, and nothing in OEIS A033950 records a resolution. Caveat: the argument is elementary enough that it may be folklore. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

Erdos308.erdos_308.variants.all_N.note: The statement (for every N>=1 the representable integers form {1..m}) is the literal Erdős–Graham question 'Let N>=1 ...'. Croot [Cr99] settled it only for sufficiently large N (ineffective o(1)), which is why erdosproblems lists #308 as 'essentially solved'. The proof is a genuine self-contained argument: a kernel-checked base case for N<=64, then an induction showing the maximal representable integer grows by at most 2 per step and that an attained maximum has an attained predecessor. I found no prior all-N proof; Chen's Nov 2026 hexagon preprint covers almost all N only. Caveat: this is a modest strengthening of an already essentially-solved problem. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

Erdos74.erdos_74.variants.sqrt.note: The statement asks for a graph with infinite chromatic number whose n-vertex subgraphs are all within sqrt(n) edge deletions of bipartite. That matches the problem page's 'open even for f(n)=sqrt n'; the max over (not necessarily induced) subgraphs is the same as over induced ones. The main #74 was disproved by GPT-6 Astra only for a very slowly growing f of order log n/log log n, which does not imply the sqrt(n) case. This self-contained disproof proves that any graph with the sqrt(n) local bound has finite chromatic number, via short odd-walk transversals, shell filtrations and ball-carving colourings. erdosproblems shows no sqrt(n) claim. The proof is credited to @preternatural-tocsin (Gemini agent). No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA69004.conjecture2.variants.without_.note: The statement (5a(n) >= pi(n) for all n>1, plus three equalities) is exactly T. D. Noe's lower bound with his claimed equalities; the upper half was already refuted at n=512720. The disproof is a genuine unconditional analytic argument. It takes n = 2^r times many primes ≡ 3 (mod 4), bounds a(n) with Selberg's Lambda^2 sieve, uses the divergence of the product of p/(p-1) over p ≡ 3 (mod 4) via finite Euler products, and uses Chebyshev's lower bound for pi(n). It concludes that 5a(n) < pi(n) for some n. I found no prior refutation of the lower bound in OEIS or upstream. Caveat: this is a minor OEIS empirical remark, and the failure was heuristically expected; the proof is non-constructive. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA179524.conjecture4.note: The statement n | sum_{k<n} (20k+17) a(k) for all n >= 1, with a(n) = sum_k (-4)^k C(n,k)^2 C(n-k,k)^2 (ℕ subtraction is harmless since k <= n), is exactly Z.-W. Sun's 2010 conjecture as recorded in OEIS A179524. The proof is a genuine argument: a telescoping identity reduces the weight, powers of 2 are handled separately, and for the odd part a q-analogue vanishes at odd-order roots of unity, with cyclotomic specialization giving divisibility. OEIS still lists it as a conjecture, and my searches (Sun's open-conjectures list, follow-up papers) found no prior proof. Caveat: Sun's congruence conjectures are heavily studied, so a prior proof in the literature cannot be fully excluded. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

OeisA79727.conjecture3.note: The statement a((p^2-1)/2) ≡ p^2 mod p^4 for primes p ≡ 3, 5, 6 mod 7 (OeisA3625.A, with a(n) = sum_{k<=n} C(2k,k)^3) is exactly Peter Bala's Conjecture 3 (July 2024) on OEIS A079727. The proof is a substantial genuine argument: a coefficient of the formal multiplication series of an elliptic curve with CM by Q(sqrt -7), related to a squared Legendre value, plus block cancellation, with p = 3 checked directly. OEIS still lists it as a conjecture (checked up to p = 101), and I found no prior proof. Caveat: the literature search was not exhaustive. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

VCDimConvex.exists_exponential_bound_has.note: HasAddVCNDimAtMost is the standard VC_n-dimension notion for translates: no (d+1)^n sum-grid is shattered. The statement asks for c >= 2 with bound c^n for every convex set in R^{n+1}. The proof gives c = 3 by proving the stronger bounds VC_n <= 2 for n >= 2 and VC_1 <= 3. It is a long, genuine argument: a self-contained Borsuk-Ulam via Ky Fan parity, convex-position cone arguments and chamber surgery. Upstream marks it open, and the only prior result is Kitamura's doubly exponential bound. Caveat: the conjecture is the formal-conjectures authors' own, with no literature source, and the same author's sibling PRs (#2797, #2823) also claim the sharper open variants. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

VCDimConvex.hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_two_of_.note: The Lean statement is exactly the question asked: for all n>=1, every convex set in R^(n+1) has VC_n dimension at most 3, using the standard HasAddVCNDimAtMost definition, which is non-trivial. The proof is a real 4,300-line argument: a Borsuk-Ulam theorem proved from scratch via Ky Fan parity, Radon for n=1, and chamber surgery for n>=3. As a by-product it proves the sharper bound VC_n <= 2 for n >= 2, which also settles the separately listed open lemma hasAddVCNDimAtMost_two_two_of_convex_r3. The PR does not claim to port earlier work. The only prior results I found are Kitamura's finite bound 2^(8(n+2)^n)-1 and his counterexample to <=1, and I found nothing in the literature on this question. Caveat: the question was posed inside formal-conjectures ('What's not in the literature'), not in a published source, and the argument has no human-written exposition. No earlier proof was found as of this review; corrections welcome.

RudinsConjecture.rudins_conjecture_uniqu.reason: The formal 'uniqueness' says that for all N>=6 every non-trivial progression attaining Qmax(N) has difference exactly 24. At N=6 the progression 120n+49 (49, 169, 289, 529) attains Q(6)=4, which refutes that claim trivially. The literature 'super-strong' conjecture of González-Jiménez–Xarles asserts uniqueness only up to equivalence and only for N = GP_k + 1 >= 8, so the formalization (all N>=6, literal q=24) is stronger than the real conjecture. The disproof exploits this mismatch and says nothing about the actual conjecture.

Bugeaud06.problem_10_6_variant_1.reason: The proof is a genuine, elementary construction: m enumerates {a*2^t : 1 <= a <= floor(log t)+1}. Density for every irrational xi follows from Dirichlet's theorem plus doubling, and consecutive ratios are >= 1 + (1/2)/log n. But Bugeaud's Problem 10.6 ('find a very rapidly increasing sequence...') is open-ended and not a precise statement. 'IsGenuinelySublacunary' (ratio floor 1 + c/log n, i.e. growth only about exp(cn/log n)) is a threshold the formalizers chose themselves, and the same argument works with any unbounded multiplier bound A(t). So it is not what Bugeaud asks, and proving it does not solve Problem 10.6. At most it settles a weak, catalogue-invented variant.

Green44.green_44.reason: The disproof only works because the formalization quantifies over all N, with no 'N sufficiently large' condition. It takes N = 100000 and the 1000 primes in [20011, 30161], which are < N^{9/10} = 31622 only because N^{1/10} < 10. Each A_i is the block of residues 10002..10001 + floor(p_i/2), so all of [1, 10001] survives and 10*|remaining| = 100010 > N. For large N (any N > 10^10) every prime is below N/10, and this trivial block trick is impossible. Green's question (from Erdős, contrasting with the large-sieve range p < N^{1/2}) is about the asymptotic regime, so nothing was learned about the real problem.

Erdos354.erdos_354.parts.ii.reason: The formal statement reads 'what if 2 is replaced by some gamma in (1,2)' as an EXISTENTIAL over gamma. The proof (a port of Kenta Kitamura's development) just picks gamma = sqrt(golden ratio) and shows that a SINGLE floor sequence floor(gamma^n alpha) is complete for every alpha>0. The second sequence and the hypothesis that alpha/beta is irrational are never used, which shows the formalization has removed the actual content of the question (whether, or for which, gamma in (1,2) the two-sequence statement holds as it does for gamma=2). This does not answer the question as erdosproblems.com poses it.

Arxiv.2507.17780.tx_graffiti_conjecture_.reason: This disproof uses a real counterexample: an explicit 50-vertex cubic graph with a maximal matching of 15 edges (every edge meets vertices 0..29), and a kernel-checked certificate that no independent dominating set has 15 or fewer vertices. So i(G)=16 > 15 >= mu*(G). The definitions (IsIndepDominating, IsMaximalEdgeMatching) are faithful. However, this 50-vertex graph with i(G)=16 > 15 = gamma_e(G) was already published as a counterexample to the TxGraffiti i(G) <= mu*(G) conjecture: a Zenodo release in 2026 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21852504), cited by Afrasyab, arXiv:2609.10783 (Sep 2026), whose abstract states it 'had been used to refute the stronger independent-domination inequality'. The upstream 'open' tag is out of date.

Erdos18.erdos_18a.reason: The formal statement matches the first ($250) question: there exist infinitely many practical m with h(m) < (log log m)^C. The proof is a real sieve/Fourier argument, but its own header says it follows Wouter van Doorn and GPT-6 Astra Pro (github.com/Woett/ChatGPT-s-note-on-Erdos18), building on Liam Price. Both are public proof claims on erdosproblems.com/18: Price, 2026-07-24, h(n) << (log log n)^2; van Doorn, 2026-09-16, with a full Lean formalisation. So this is a re-formalisation of an already-claimed result, not a new one.

Erdos252.erdos_252.variants.k_ge_five.reason: The file proves irrationality of sum sigma_k(n)/n! for every k, specialised to k>=5. The argument is real: factorial tails become integers under rationality, a Stirling expansion, and CRT-aligned dilations giving unequal progression means. The file states it is adapted from github.com/tokengr1nder/Erdos252. That exact proof (with its Lean formalisation) was posted as a proof claim on erdosproblems.com/252 on 2026-09-08, before this PR (2026-11-27). The statement is faithful, but the result is not new to this submission.

Erdos488.erdos_488.reason: This is a genuine counterexample for the 'multiples' reading of #488, with 0,1 excluded as in formal-conjectures PR 256. The set A consists of 257-smooth numbers in (T,256T], and the density more than doubles between n and m. The file says it is adapted from Alicien B.'s Lean disproof (github.com/Alicienn/erdos-488-lean; paper aixiv 2611.02020v2). The same kind of counterexample was posted as a Lean-checked proof claim by Declan Gessel on erdosproblems.com/488 on 2026-09-05. Not a new result.

Erdos676.erdos_676.reason: The statement (n = a p^2 + b, p prime, a>=1, 0<=b<p, eventually) faithfully renders #676, and the disproof (a dyadic sieve plus moment estimates giving >> X/log X exceptions in (X,2X]) is a real argument. The file is explicitly a port of the earlier disproof by Will Howe, Grant Huffman, Jensen Kohlmeyer and Liam Kruer (github.com/Ghuffy1/erdos676, Lean endpoint Erdos676.erdos676_negative; their review is still pending). The result therefore predates this PR. It is not yet recorded on erdosproblems.com, which still lists the problem as open.

Erdos786.erdos_786.parts.ii.reason: The formal IsMulCardSet uses Finsets, i.e. distinct factors, which is the version erdosproblems.com says is still open. With repetitions the answer is classically no (ERS73). The disproof shows |A| < (1-eta)N for admissible A. It is adapted from daizisheng/erdos-786, which is Shisheng Li's proof claim on erdosproblems.com/786 (2026-09-28, 'both formal-conjectures statements are proved in Lean'). Erdős [Er80] also attributes a negative answer to Ruzsa. Not new.

Erdos97.erdos_97.reason: The file is a declared mechanical port of Kruer, Kohlmeyer and Price, 'Unit distances in convex polygons' (13 Sep 2026, github.com/lkruer/erdos-96-97-proof). Their construction gives convex polygons where every vertex has >> log log n vertices at distance 1. erdosproblems.com/97 already marks the problem as false and links that formalised proof, and the batch's own erdosState is 'disproved'.

Fuglede.FugledeConjecture.variants.dim_2.reason: This formalises the 'spectral but does not tile' direction of T. Zhang, 'Both directions of Fuglede's conjecture fail in dimension two', arXiv:2607.15632 (July 2026). The set is the lift of a 60-point subset of Z_60 x Z_12 to a finite union of unit squares. The proof is genuine and the statement is faithful, but the upstream docstring itself cites Zhang's announced negative answer. Already known (preprint, unrefereed).

MonochromaticQuantumGraph.eqSystem10_no_.reason: The proof is a one-line specialisation of OMA.krennGuAllOrders, a port of Rishi Rajasekaran's Lean proof of the full Krenn-Gu statement (no complex solution for all even N>=6, D>=3; github.com/rrajasek95/krenn-conjecture). That proof was submitted as formal-conjectures PR #6627 on 2026-09-26 and is cited in arXiv:2611.26300 [40] ('discovered a proof of the entire conjecture... formally verified via Lean'). The EqSystemN encoding (one weight per vertex pair and endpoint colours, mono=1, non-mono=0) is a faithful encoding of the GHZ condition. Not new.

The file is byte-identical to PR 2627 except for the final line: the same port of Rajasekaran's all-orders Krenn-Gu proof, instantiated at N=10, D=7. The general result was submitted to formal-conjectures (PR #6627, 2026-09-26) and cited in arXiv:2611.26300. Not new.

MonochromaticQuantumGraph.eqSystem6_no_s.reason: This is again the port of Rajasekaran's all-orders proof (formal-conjectures PR #6627, cited in arXiv:2611.26300), specialised to N=6. Even apart from that, the N=6 case was already covered by recorded solved results: D=3 (algal certificate), D=4 (KitaKen1), and D>=5 via the sharp bound D<=N-2 [Ki26], all listed as solved in the upstream file.

MonochromaticQuantumGraph.eqSystem_no_so.reason: The real-weight version follows from Rajasekaran's complex all-orders proof by mapping matching sums through the real-to-complex ring homomorphism. The file says it adapts the palette restriction of an earlier PR. This is a faithful and genuine argument, but the underlying complex result (formal-conjectures PR #6627, 2026-09-26; arXiv:2611.26300 ref [40]) predates it.

OeisA251758.conjecture.reason: The statement (IsLeast of {x>=2 : a(x)=8} at p#12/p#4 = 35336848261, with primeCounting' 8 = 4) faithfully encodes Wilson's 2014 question. The proof is real: it bounds a(x) for all x < X0. But the file declares itself adapted from Pablo Santana Torres's repository pablodrake/oeis-a251758, an earlier Lean proof of exactly this formal-conjectures statement. That repository also cites an earlier computational argument (Oct 4, 2026, trureturing issue #12805). Not new to this PR.

OeisA92243.conjecture1.reason: The proof exhibits n=261150 with a(n)=1 via a kernel-checked prime-scan certificate. The definition matches OEIS (primeGap k = p_{k+1}-p_k, 1-indexed). However, the answer was already in the OEIS entry itself: N. J. A. Sloane's linked table a092243_1.txt (n up to 965562) lists '261150 1' and several other positive values just above 250000. So the question 'is a(n)>0 for some n>250000?' was already answered by existing data.

AtiyahSutcliffe.conjecture_one.reason: The formal statement is faithful. The unnormalized stereographic lift only rescales each linear factor, and linear independence is invariant under nonzero rescaling and under the uniform Mobius/antipodal change of convention. The proof exhibits an explicit 69-point planar configuration on a one-parameter path, and a sign change of a projected 2x2 determinant (exact arithmetic in Q(sqrt2, sqrt362)) forces a linear dependence. The file says it formalizes Jan Eickhoff, 'Singular Atiyah Configurations', arXiv:2610.33090 (Oct 2026), whose abstract states that it disproves Atiyah's conjecture with configurations that include planar ones. So the disproof is real but already published.

Erdos111.erdos_111.reason: The statement is faithful: hG is the sup over n-vertex induced subgraphs of the minimum number of edge deletions that make the subgraph bipartite, which is exactly h_G(n), and all such values are bounded by C(n,2). The file openly ports Plasma AI's proof (github.com/plasma-ai/erdos-111, Palomar entry PALOMAR-2026-10-19-000007): a graph whose finite subgraphs are C-linear is countably colourable, which gives h_G(n)/n -> infinity. The bridge to the formal-conjectures definitions is a genuine argument. erdosproblems.com still shows the problem as open, but the result was first established and published by Plasma AI in October 2026.

Erdos18.erdos_18b.reason: The statement h(n!) < n^eps eventually matches erdosproblems.com/18 part (b), and practicalH correctly allows a fresh set of divisors for each m. The proof derives a bound h(n!) = O((log n)^5) via binary tries and shifted digit sets. The file itself credits Kohlmeyer and Kruer with proving part (b) in September 2026, and Howe, Huffman, Kohlmeyer and Kruer with the (log n)^9 bound (public repository Ghuffy1/erdos18-harmonic-shifts). Part (b) was therefore already settled.

Erdos307.erdos_307.variants.coprime_one_.reason: The variant is stated faithfully: pairwise coprime P and Q, each with at least 2 elements, 1 not in either set, product of reciprocal sums equal to 1 (the clause '0 not in P intersect Q' is harmless). The proof gives an explicit witness: Q = {2,3,7,41}, plus 54 primes below 280 extended by a kernel-checked chain of huge deviation elements. Both PRs credit Doug Phillips, who announced the first such sets on 26 Nov 2026 (github.com/duggiephresh/unit-fraction-solutions, Palomar entry PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000045). erdosproblems.com still says no example is known, but the example predates these PRs.

Erdos510.erdos_510.reason: The formal statement (absolute c>0 such that eventually every N-set A of positive integers has min of the cosine sum < -c sqrt N) is the Chowla N^{1/2} question. The disproof uses a theorem giving, for every eps>0, arbitrarily large A with every cosine sum > -eps sqrt|A|, which genuinely refutes it. The file is an inlined port of Shengtong Zhang's public counterexample (github.com/shengtongz/chowla-cosine-counterexample; manuscript produced by an AI model prompted by Zhang), so it is prior work.

Erdos700.erdos_700.parts.ii.reason: The statement (infinitely many composite n with f(n)^2 > n, where f(n) is the min over 1<k<=n/2 of gcd(n, C(n,k))) is faithful. The disproof is genuine: for an explicit odd offset g, every 2^n+g is divisible by a prime from each of two disjoint covering sets, with pq < g, so it is never a semiprime and g is never a value of a. The OEIS entry records no answer. However, the content is an immediate corollary of a known result: PR 2268 uses exactly Arkadiusz Wesolowski's published doubly-covered Sierpinski number (primepuzzles problem 92: k*2^n+1 always has at least 3 distinct prime factors), and the standard exponent-reversal trick (as in Filaseta-Groth-Luckner 2023, Cor. 4.1) transfers the covering to k+2^n. It is a valid answer to an idle OEIS question, not a new theorem.

OeisA60841.conjecture1.reason: The statement (1/det of the 1/lcm(i,j) matrix is an integer exactly for n in 1..34, 36, 38) is faithful to the first assertion of Wilson's conjecture. WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture84.con.reason: The statement (connected G with positive minimum degree satisfies tree(G) >= 2 rad(G)/delta(G)) matches WOWII #84; the hypothesis delta>0 is harmless. Gebendorfer's manuscript 'Induced trees in graphs with a cut vertex: A proof of WOWII Conjecture 84' (28 Oct 2026, posted as formal-conjectures issue #7663). The result is prior work.

Green41.green_41.variants.double_exponen.reason: Port of an earlier proof by other authors (see the PR and the reviewer notes); the result is not new to this submission. Erdos895.erdos_895.variants.hindman.reason: The proof is a genuine idempotent-ultrafilter plus compactness argument: for each k, every triangle-free graph on [1,n] with n large has an independent finite-sums set FS(a_1..a_k) with distinct a_i. The [1,n] version follows by compactness. The infinite Hindman version was answered negatively by Deuber-Gunderson-Hindman-Strauss (1997). The erdosproblems.com remark that this 'remains open' appears to be out of date.
